correctness.rationale: For a>0 on the unit round S², applying the Legendre recurrence three times gives only degrees n±3 and n±1 in T₃Pₙ; the displayed four rational coefficients are positive for n≥3, and at n=2 the lower outer term is absent. At n=0 and n=1 the negative coefficients are respectively −3/5 at degree 1 and −1/5 at degree 0. Normalization at 1 gives the convex combinations; the absolutely summable nonnegative expansion justifies applying the multiplier to the whole supported cone. The exponential moment recurrence follows by integrating the Legendre derivative identity and the angular Sturm–Liouville equation; the boundary terms are zero (the derivative difference vanishes at the endpoints and the latter equation has a sin(θ) factor). Together with A₀ and A₁ this gives every Aₙ>0. Independently, exp(−a arccos t)=exp(−aπ/2)exp(a arcsin t) has a convergent nonnegative power series on [−1,1] with all monomial coefficients positive; the tⁿ term contributes positively to Pₙ and powers of t have nonnegative Legendre coefficients by recurrence. The mixed-product expansion thus forces Bₙ>0 for n≥2. The elementary sin(4θ)−sin(2θ) and sin(5θ)−sin(θ) integrals give the signs of B₀ and B₁ as those of a²−8 and a²−5, respectively. Schoenberg's criterion gives the iff including its endpoint; all positive degrees survive there, so both parities are infinite and strict positive definiteness follows. At equality all RKHS elements have zero mean, while above it the RKHS contains all finite spherical harmonic sums, giving exactly the stated uniform-density transition.
